clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-913, measured. For each network, the gas cap of a mined ordinary transaction, and the gas of a full liquidity exit of a real position by its real owner at the real PoolManager, compared with that cap and not with the eth_call limit.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The code claim holds under my reading. Pool.modifyLiquidity (src/libraries/Pool.sol:145-238) has no loop: two updateTick calls (Pool.sol:158-160), at most two flipTick calls (Pool.sol:173-178), one position update (Pool.sol:182-187), clearTick by delete (Pool.sol:192-199, 592-594) and one liquidity write (Pool.sol:226). Position.update (src/libraries/Position.sol:76-101) writes liquidity and the two fee growth words; the only fresh writes it can make are those two words, so the worst case is bounded per position and another account cannot grow it. One wording point: whether those two words go from zero to nonzero depends on swaps by others, but that is at most two fresh slots in any case, which the item already allows for. I confirmed the smallest cap link for HyperEVM from its docs (fast blocks 1 second with a 3M gas limit, slow blocks 30M) and the Arbitrum cap by my own eth_call. The largest sampled exit (Tempo, 976,067) is far below Tempo's 30,000,000. The cast feesOwed.toInt128() at Pool.sol:186 can revert an exit only if owed fees exceed int128, which is not a gas matter and is not reachable at realistic fee volumes.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Claim redemption under the mined cap: burn(holder, id, balance) and take(currency, holder, balance) by real ERC-6909 holders at the real PoolManager, run with a gas limit of 16,777,216 (3,000,000 on HyperEVM).
clearedSpotChecks.note: burn (src/PoolManager.sol:332-336) is one _accountDelta and _burnFrom, which writes an allowance only when the caller is neither the owner nor an operator and the allowance is not max (src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22). take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) is one _accountDelta and one currency transfer. No loop and no state another account can grow, so the measured values (at most 134,721) generalise. The seven unmeasured networks stay an open low lead as the item says; the gas bound comes from the code and does not depend on the measurement.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Mined cap on the Arbitrum family, read from ArbGasInfo, and the Monad and Tempo caps.
clearedSpotChecks.note: My eth_call 0x612af178 to 0x...006C on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc returned 0x6acfc0 (7,000,000), 0x1e84800 (32,000,000) and 0x1e84800 (32,000,000), matching speedLimit, gasPoolMax and maxTxGasLimit. https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/gas-pricing lists a 150M gas block limit and a 30M gas transaction limit, as stated. On Tempo, eth_estimateGas for a value-less call to an empty address returned 0x42f8e (274,318) with both 30,000,000 and 30,000,001 as the gas field, which shows the fresh account cost but does not by itself test the 30,000,000 cap; the TIP-1010 link I did not fetch. With exits at most 976,067 the cap value does not change the conclusion. The MegaETH SALT cost model rests on F-105's rule and was not re-derived here.
